proposed_fixes.title: Identify and handle the Runner termination path before changing shutdown behavior
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Low-confidence hypothesis: an external Windows session-end or close-app request may terminate Runner while Command Palette survives as a separate process. The archive does not rule out an internal exit or another external source.
plan: Use the newer investigation's session-end logging to distinguish WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION from crash or internal shutdown evidence.
Trace tray_icon_window_proc and handle_stateless_session_end_message without changing existing return behavior.
If logs prove an unintended request, make the narrowest lifecycle change that preserves legitimate shutdown and update semantics.
If logs show an internal failure, fix that concrete path instead of changing session-end handling.
Add a regression or repeatable lifecycle test for the confirmed termination reason.
verification: Reproduce after upgrading to current stable and capture /bugreport immediately after Runner disappears.
Correlate Runner logs, Windows session events, and Command Palette liveness.
Verify Runner and tools remain available during the reported workload while normal logoff, shutdown, and update flows still work.

confidence.rationale: The process split and Runner message path are confirmed, but the archive has no crash or termination proof and no behavioral fix can be selected honestly yet.

design.root_cause: Unconfirmed external or internal Runner termination; a session-end or close-app request is plausible but unproven.
evidence: Observed: Runner/tray disappears while Command Palette remains active.
Observed: the available archive has no direct PowerToys.exe crash entry.
Observed: tray_icon_window_proc dispatches session-end messages through handle_stateless_session_end_message.
Observed: draft PR 50273 adds session-end reason and confirmation logging.
Inferred: separate process lifetimes explain the surviving Command Palette but not the Runner exit.

affected_files.purpose: Owns the Runner tray window procedure and dispatches Windows session-end messages before normal message handling.
Provides the Restart Manager integration area to compare external close requests with session-end behavior.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The tray window procedure forwards session-end messages to handle_stateless_session_end_message and returns the handler result; the available archive does not show whether this path caused the observed exit.
implementation_steps.change: Capture a fresh failure with reason-specific logging, then change this path only if evidence proves an unintended session-end or close-app request. Preserve legitimate OS shutdown semantics.
tests: Add or run a focused lifecycle test for the confirmed termination reason and normal session shutdown.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Restart Manager is a plausible external close source, but the current issue archive does not correlate a Restart Manager event with Runner disappearance.
implementation_steps.change: Compare Restart Manager evidence with the fresh Runner/session-end logs; modify this integration only if it is the confirmed termination source.
tests: Verify normal update and Restart Manager close/restart flows after any cause-specific change.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: No regression test currently establishes that Runner remains available while Command Palette continues as a separate process during the reported workload.
implementation_steps.change: After the termination cause is known, add repeatable lifecycle coverage that distinguishes Runner exit from the independent Command Palette process lifetime.
tests: Repeat the reported workload and verify Runner, tray state, and PowerToys tools remain available when no legitimate termination request occurs.

verify: Correlate logs and OS events at the next disappearance.
Repeat the same workload after the cause-specific change.
Confirm normal logoff, shutdown, update, and Restart Manager flows remain unaffected.
risks: Suppressing legitimate session-end or close-app handling could leave stale processes or interfere with updates.
Changing Runner lifetime behavior without distinguishing Command Palette's separate process could mask the cause.
alternatives: Consolidate with Issue 50169 and collect reason-specific logs; preferred over a speculative fix.
Treat it as a crash; not supported by the available archive, though new evidence could change that.
